sources.quote: The habit of going vegan and visiting pagodas on the first and fifteenth days of each lunar month dates back from the Ly dynasty (1010-1225) as Buddhism grew very strong then.
Having vegetarian food on the first and 15th day of a lunar month or four times a month has become a habit among Buddhists.

Lay Buddhists adopt "temporary" vegetarianism on preassigned dates as a rite of abstinence or purification. They eat vegetarian as a reminder to avoid doing or saying bad things and to increase good luck for themselves, their families, and their ancestors for the new month.
Both Mahayana Buddhists and Cao Đài followers practice vegetarianism for similar reasons: to cultivate compassion
